trends.title: Sinaloa civil war: Chapitos vs Mayiza
trends.context: The split between El Chapo's sons (Chapitos) and the Zambada faction (Mayiza), now in its second year, has spread from Culiacán to Mazatlán, southern Sinaloa and neighbouring states. It drives the highest sustained violence in Mexico and shapes who controls Pacific fentanyl and cocaine routes.

developments.text: A Navy-led operation killed 'El Meny Carranza', a regional priority target that El Heraldo describes as a Chapitos ally, and arrested four; days later Sonora prosecutors held 'El Chore' of a cell aligned with a Sinaloa faction, placing federal pressure on the war's Sonora flank.

trends.title: CJNG: regional commanders face parallel Mexican and US prosecution
trends.context: CJNG is Mexico's most widely spread cartel. Mexican and US authorities now build parallel cases against its regional commanders, while it keeps fighting rivals in Michoacán, Veracruz and the Isthmus.

developments.text: A US grand jury indicted 'El Tanque' Iván Cazarín Molina, a regional CJNG operator, as a Mexican judge threw out his injunction and Veracruz prosecutors added the Las Bajadas massacre: one man facing parallel Mexican and US cases.

trends.title: Terrorist labels, extraditions and US scrutiny
trends.context: Since the US listed major cartels as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, allied governments have copied the labels and extraditions have sped up. The labels change the legal and financial exposure of anyone who does business with these groups.

developments.text: Two Argentine court cases behind the new listing show different Mexican footholds: a Bolivia-based Sinaloa branch flying cocaine into Salta for export to Europe through Paraná river ports, and a small CJNG cell that tested a Belgium-to-Zárate MDMA shipment paid through hawala and crypto; specialists found no documented La Nueva Familia Michoacana presence, so the label outruns the evidence for that group.

trends.title: Ecuador: Los Lobos vs Los Choneros
trends.context: Los Lobos and Los Choneros are fighting over Ecuador's cocaine export corridor, from prisons to the Manabí and Guayas coast. Inside the state, police and prison staff collude with the gangs.

developments.text: Two new prison massacres left at least eight inmates dead: the prisons are still a front in the gang war.

trends.context: Tren de Aragua spread from Venezuela's prisons into a network of extortion and sexual-exploitation cells across the Andes and Chile. Its cells now face prosecution in the countries they moved into.

developments.text: InSight Crime traces TdA's rise in Lima to extortion of sex workers, with killings of those who refused to pay: its money comes from local predation, not just trafficking.

trends.title: Haiti: gangs over the state
trends.context: The Viv Ansanm gang coalition controls most of Port-au-Prince and has repeatedly blocked the political transition. Neighbours and the anti-gang force respond on security terms.

developments.text: Foreign Minister Víctor Bisonó said Dominican troops are staying out of the international military operations against Haiti's gangs, offering only diplomatic, humanitarian and logistical support: Santo Domingo is militarising its own side of the border while keeping out of the fight inside Haiti.
